svg.title: CSPflow full workflow tutorial
svg.desc: A numbered beginner tutorial showing how to create, configure, validate, run, monitor, and report a CSPflow crystal structure prediction campaign.
svg.text: BEGINNER MAP · CONFIGURE → CHECK → RUN → REPORT
One campaign folder. Three YAML controls. Eight stages. Reproducible results.

g.text: Phase B is the costly part
Init asks whether to recompute references.
Editable copies; the folder is the campaign.
The template is examples/<N>-*/ — each type starts a different funnel.
You edit element groups; cspflow enumerates formulas.
No demo input files · largest size multiplier
Inline items and CSV can be used together.
Replace the Sm–Fe files in inputs/seeds/.
No generate block or source.defaults · enters at screen
MENU / SAFE STOP: csp init test asks interactively; scripts exit and write nothing. csp init 7 test or csp init 2 prints the menu + correct usage.
Start with campaign.yaml; change the other two only for cluster or DFT policy.
filter hull cut · composition / symmetry caps
Only live, type-aligned settings are in each example.
Roles keep campaigns portable between clusters.
retry: ordered remedies for known failures
OPTION MAP · magnetism: ferrimagnetic_retm | ferromagnetic | table | pymatgen | none · f-electrons: frozen | valence · layout: runs | stages · combined_job: true | false
Resolved settings are what you intended
Cheap preparation runs to completion first.
structure_list enters at screen; generation is automatically skipped.
Ctrl-C stops the watcher safely; run the same command to resume.
Read comments, preview the result, then run only what you intend.
Several key-value pairs use commas inside { }.
Keep indentation. Unknown keys are rejected.
Ctrl-C is safe; submitted jobs continue. Run again to resume.
Settings: docs/06-settings.md · DFT recipes: docs/09-recipes.md · Command reference: docs/12-cli.md
